blocks.content: The Governor acts as a vital bridge between the Centre and the State, exercising constitutional functions with specified discretionary powers.

rows: Can pardon, reprieve, or commute death sentences and military court-martial sentences (Article 72).
Cannot pardon death sentences or court-martial sentences, but can suspend, remit, or commute them (Article 161).
Promulgates ordinances under Article 123 when Parliament is not in session.
Promulgates ordinances under Article 213 when the State Legislature is not in session.
Has situational discretion but no express constitutional discretionary powers.
Has explicit constitutional discretionary powers granted under Article 163.

items: An ordinance promulgated by the Governor under Article 213 must be approved by the state legislature within six weeks from its reassembly.
The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence under Article 161; only the President holds the authority to pardon death sentences under Article 72.
The validity of any action taken by the Governor in their discretion cannot be called into question in any court of law under Article 163.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Governor is the constitutional head of the state executive, functioning as a vital link between the Central Government and the State.
Under Article 213, the Governor has the legislative power to promulgate ordinances when the State Legislature is not in session.
Unlike the President, the Governor possesses explicit constitutional discretionary powers under Article 163.
The Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment under Article 161, but lacks the power to pardon a death sentence.
All executive actions of the state government are formally taken in the name of the Governor.
